incidents.name: BBT token unprotected setRegistry enables unlimited mint
incidents.notes: BBT.setRegistry(address) had no access control, so the attacker pointed the token at a registry contract of their own whose getContractAddress() returned the caller, passing the mint() authorization check and minting 1e31 BBT that was dumped on Uniswap V2.

sources.ref: onchain review: TransparentUpgradeableProxy 0x3541499cda8CA51B24724Bb8e7Ce569727406E04 created 2024-01-18 by 0xb0ab5d6f8e99c07fa4965524bbe9c57d9ed35a38, not the attack-tx sender; three EIP-1967 Upgraded events, the last at block 19113181 on 2024-01-29T15:49:35Z installing 0x74463ed91bfa45bca06d59e8b383a89709842f69, so the executing code was 42.7 days old. 5.06 ETH at a March 2024 ETH price near $4,000 is roughly $20k, above the $1,000 floor. Loss converted at the incident timestamp: 5.06 ETH x $3,972.80 (DefiLlama historical ETH price) = $20,102.
